intelligence.enrichment: The Moon keeps its shape and shines by reflected sunlight; phases are the changing shapes of the illuminated part visible from Earth. Sunlight illuminates half of the Moon -> Earth sees only the illuminated part facing Earth -> the visible bright shape changes. The learner correctly applies this rule: The Moon keeps its shape and shines by reflected sunlight; phases are the changing shapes of the illuminated part visible from Earth. The Moon's shape changes each night, and shadows or the Moon's own light make the changing shapes.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: The night sky: Moon and calendars. The student must decide: Decide that Moon phases are changes in the bright part seen from Earth, not changes in the Moon's own shape or light. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
